Travel Reimbursement Form (GAD Form X-5)

From the ORA eTraining module "Travel on Sponsored Projects: From Approval to Reimbursement" (lesson 6 of 8).
How To: Completing a Travel Reimbursement Form
Grant-Funded Travelers should use the Travel Reimbursement Form DocuSign found here .
sm
When to Submit
Reimbursement requests should be submitted within 5 business days of the traveler's return.
Expenses to Include
On this form make sure to only include on this form those expenses which need to be reimbursed. Expenses paid by purchase order or p-card should not be listed on the reimbursement form.
Commute Miles
The form requires entry of commute miles if you are requesting mileage reimbursement. Total mileage reimbursement will be reduced by the traveler's commute mileage on travel days when they would typically work (commonly Monday - Friday).
Meal Per Diem
Receipts are not required for meal per diem reimbursement. A traveler can only request per diem based on their travel times. For example, here John Doe left his home at 12:30pm and does not qualify for breakfast on Tuesday July 1st. Review the travel guidance on per diem rates covered in the "How to Complete a TL Form" lesson in this module.
Meal Per Diem (In-State Travel)
If traveling in-state, a traveler can only request per diem if they leave their home 2 hours earlier than usual AND return home 2 hours later than usual.
Taxi Reimbursement
Taxi and rideshare charges can be reimbursed if receipts are provided to the MSU Travel Office. Tips will be reimbursed up to 20% of the total fare cost.
Mileage Reimbursement
Mileage reimbursement is automatically calculated based on figures entered on the second table of this form. The mileage rate changes every fiscal year. A mileage map is required for mileage reimbursement requests. See example below in this lesson.
Total Reimbursement
The total amount to be reimbursed to the traveler is listed here ($478.11). This figure may be reduced by the Travel Office if a travel advance was requested. If the advance exceeds the total reimbursement the difference must be returned to the Bursar's Office.
Travel Times
Travel times are important for several reasons. The University needs to know when the traveler is covered by MSU's insurance. It is also vital in per diem calculations.
Commute Miles (Continued)
As mentioned above, mileage reimbursement requests do not need to factor in commute mileage if it is a non-standard working day. In our example, John came back from travel on Sunday so he is entitled to the full mileage reimbursement.
Agency Code
Morgan State University's Agency Code is 36.13.00. You will use this code for any MSU-funded travel reimbursement.

Most reimbursement requests should be accompanied by an authorized TL form. One exception exists: in-state travel without lodging expenses. In that case, include the 6-digit budget index and travel account code (04XXX) on the reimbursement form.
Authorized TL Form
If you are requesting mileage reimbursement. A printout of Google Maps or MapQuest works fine.
Mileage Map
You will need original receipts if requesting reimbursement of expenses such as hotel, parking fees, tolls, taxi/rideshare, baggage fees, etc. Receipts are not needed for meal per diem expenses.
Original Receipts
If you request reimbursement for out-of-pocket expenses you may be required to submit a redacted copy of your personal card statement. The statement must include your name, address, last 4 digits of card used, and expense detail.
Redacted Credit Card Statement
Only for group travel activity. If applicable, please note the travel advance provided to each student.
Attendee List
Only if a travel advance was requested by the traveler.
Check Stub
The State of Maryland now requires a travel itinerary for each reimbursement request. Either (a) a self drafted itinerary of travel times/events or (b) a conference-supplied itinerary is appropriate.
